review_notes: Read the entire target file (794 lines) and checked each declaration against Mathlib/Batteries/core. Relevant supporting sources inspected: OAI/Computability/MinUncut/PCP/Walsh.lean (Cube, bitSign, cubeXor, walsh, coefficient), OAI/Computability/MinUncut/Encoding/ThreeBitTest.lean (support, noiseWeight, thirdQuery, testAcceptance), Batteries List.product, Mathlib/Data/List/ProdSigma.lean, Mathlib/Data/List/Defs.lean (SProd instance), Mathlib/Algebra/Notation/Pi/Basic.lean (Pi.mulSingle/Pi.single, mulSingle_apply), Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/BooleanRing.lean (Zero/One/Add Bool), and several sibling files that copy the same cart/coordinateMask code. Searched Mathlib and core/Batteries for countP_const/countP_product/countP lemmas about List.product: none exist, so count_cart, count_cart_left/right, count_cart_le, count_const, count_union_le, count_remove appear to be genuinely new theorem-level API and were not reported (theorems are also out of scope). Other definitions (cubeFlip, HalfCube, representative, canonicalInput, foldedAnswer, restrictQuery, conditionedFoldedAnswer, allAgree, Equation, satisfied, clone, cloneList, Address, storedAssignment, rhsCorrection, equation, conditionedEquation, mapEquation, pairedEquations) were checked and are domain-specific or acceptable named specialisations/Sum.elim wrappers, not duplicates of installed concepts. Uncertainty: I could not compile, so the proposed redefinitions are suggestions only; in particular the Pi.single-based version of coordinateMask is propositionally (not syntactically) equal to decide (j = i) and existing simp [coordinateMask] proofs in walsh_coordinateMask/restrictQuery_cubeToggle would need adapting, possibly using Bool.add_eq_xor/zero_eq_false.

findings.excerpt:
def cart (xs : List α) (ys : List β) : List (α × β) :=
  xs.flatMap fun x => ys.map fun y => (x, y)
findings.problem: cart is character-for-character the definition of Batteries' List.product, which Mathlib re-exports with the ×ˢ notation and a full API. The file then re-proves product API: length_cart (lines 223-226) is exactly Mathlib's List.length_product, and triples (line 267) is literally indices ×ˢ (indices ×ˢ indices). Because cart is a fresh name, none of Mathlib's List.product lemmas (product_cons, mem_product, length_product) apply, and users must unfold cart by hand (the file's own count_cart proof has to `simp only [cart, List.flatMap_cons, ...]`). The same definition and its lemma block are also copied verbatim in at least three sibling files (e.g. OAI/Computability/VertexCover/Reduction/CloneGap.lean:41 and OAI/Computability/UniqueGames/Reduction/ActualCanonicalLemmas.lean:247), and one of them has to restate Mathlib's mem_product as mem_cart, showing the concrete conversion cost.
findings.proposed_change: Define cart as an abbreviation of List.product (`abbrev cart (xs : List α) (ys : List β) : List (α × β) := xs ×ˢ ys`) or replace its uses with `×ˢ` directly, drop length_cart in favour of List.length_product, and restate the genuinely new counting lemmas (count_cart, count_cart_left, count_cart_right, count_cart_le) about `xs ×ˢ ys`. Keep the existing names as thin wrappers if downstream files depend on them.
findings.benefit: Users get Mathlib's product lemmas (mem_product, product_cons, length_product) for free instead of unfolding flatMap, the duplicated length lemma disappears, and the many in-repo copies of cart collapse onto one standard notation.

evidence.excerpt: def product (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : List β) : List (α × β) := l₁.flatMap fun a => l₂.map (Prod.mk a)

instance instSProd : SProd (List α) (List β) (List (α × β)) where
  sprod := List.product

theorem length_product (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : List β) :
    length (l₁ ×ˢ l₂) = length l₁ * length l₂

theorem mem_product {l₁ : List α} {l₂ : List β} {a : α} {b : β} :
    (a, b) ∈ l₁ ×ˢ l₂ ↔ a ∈ l₁ ∧ b ∈ l₂

theorem length_cart (xs : List α) (ys : List β) :
    (cart xs ys).length = xs.length * ys.length := by

def cart (xs : List α) (ys : List β) : List (α × β) :=
  xs.flatMap fun x => ys.map fun y => (x, y)

findings.problem: With Mathlib's Boolean-ring structure on Bool (Zero := false, One := true, Add := xor, imported by `import Mathlib`), the standard basis vector Pi.single i true is definitionally the function `fun j => if j = i then true else false`, i.e. exactly coordinateMask i. cubeToggle is then addition of that basis vector in the Pi group (cubeXor is pointwise xor). The file re-implements this concept under a new name and never states a bridge to Pi.single, so Mathlib's Pi.single API (Pi.single_eq_same, Pi.single_eq_of_ne, Pi.single_apply, Pi.single_add) cannot be used; for instance walsh_coordinateMask (lines 111-119) has to redo Finset.prod_eq_single by hand with `simp [coordinateMask, hj, bitSign]`, and the identical definition plus the same four lemmas are copied verbatim in several sibling files (OAI/Computability/VertexCover/Fourier/Folding.lean:101, OAI/Computability/MaxCut/PCP/Folding.lean:103, OAI/Computability/UniqueGames/PCP/SourceNoiseParameterLemmas.lean:429, among others), which shows the repeated-conversion cost.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the readable name but define it through the existing operation, e.g. `def coordinateMask (i : I) : Cube I := Pi.single i true` (with `M := fun _ => Bool`), and likewise record `cubeToggle i f = f + Pi.single i true`. If changing the body is too invasive for existing `simp [coordinateMask]` proofs, add a bridge lemma `coordinateMask_eq_single : coordinateMask i = Pi.single i true` and use `Pi.single_apply`/`Pi.single_eq_same`/`Pi.single_eq_of_ne` in walsh_coordinateMask and restrictQuery_cubeToggle.
findings.benefit: The mask becomes an instance of a canonical Mathlib notion with a large generic API, so users can rewrite coordinates with Pi.single lemmas instead of unfolding `decide`, and the convention is no longer independently reinvented in each copy of the Fourier/folding development.

evidence.excerpt: def mulSingle (i : ι) (x : M i) : ∀ j, M j := Function.update 1 i x

lemma mulSingle_apply (i : ι) (x : M) (i' : ι) :
    (mulSingle i x : ι → M) i' = if i' = i then x else 1
instance : Zero Bool where zero := false

theorem walsh_coordinateMask (s : Cube I) (i : I) :
    walsh s (coordinateMask i) = bitSign (s i) := by
def coordinateMask (i : I) : Cube I := fun j => decide (j = i)
